Candidate-ranking cross-entropy over one positive and K negatives is L=−s_pos+logsumexp(s_pos,s_neg1,…,s_negK): negatives compete through one denominator. Multi-negative BCE instead uses independent sigmoid terms. PyTorch’s default BCE mean averages all K+1 terms; positive-mean plus negative-mean BCE gives equal aggregate weight to the two groups. Summed-negative BCE increases negative weight as K grows. Thus matching K alone does not match weighting or gradient scale. For a controlled NextItNet comparison, share sampled candidates, valid training positions and batch normalization; state the exact reduction and monitor gradient norms. These implications follow from the documented [CE](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.CrossEntropyLoss.html) and [BCE](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.BCEWithLogitsLoss.html) formulas.

Uniform sampling without replacement supplies K distinct negatives from an eligible pool of M items, each with inclusion probability K/M. Excluding the user’s complete public training history avoids assigning observed positives negative labels, but changes the learning objective relative to target-only exclusion; keep that policy identical across losses, exclude padding and the current target, and never consult held-out interactions. These are experimental-design implications, not evidence that one exclusion policy improves HR@10.

Uncorrected candidate CE is not automatically corrected sampled softmax. The latter accounts for sampling through log expected-count corrections; corrections must match the actual sampler, including uniqueness and exclusions. For example, when the positive is always included and negatives are uniformly selected, their inclusion probabilities differ, so a common correction need not cancel across all logits. TensorFlow documents expected-count inputs, accidental-hit removal and finite-sample approximation limitations in its [sampled-softmax API](https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/nn/sampled_softmax_loss) and [candidate-sampling reference](https://www.tensorflow.org/extras/candidate_sampling.pdf).
